id: Practice Direction 37 – Miscellaneous Provisions About Payments Into Court
content:
# PRACTICE DIRECTION 37 – MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS ABOUT PAYMENTS INTO COURT

# This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37] Contents of this Practice Direction

## PAYMENT INTO COURT UNDER AN ORDER, ETC

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > PAYMENT INTO COURT UNDER AN ORDER, ETC] 1.1 Except where paragraph 1.2 applies, a party paying money into court under an order or in support of a defence of tender before claim must –

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > PAYMENT INTO COURT UNDER AN ORDER, ETC] (1) send to the Court Funds Office –

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > PAYMENT INTO COURT UNDER AN ORDER, ETC] (a) the payment, usually a cheque made payable to the Accountant General of the Senior Courts;

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > PAYMENT INTO COURT UNDER AN ORDER, ETC] (b) a sealed copy of the order or a copy of the defence; and

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > PAYMENT INTO COURT UNDER AN ORDER, ETC] (c) a completed Court Funds Office form 100;

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > PAYMENT INTO COURT UNDER AN ORDER, ETC] (2) serve a copy of the form 100 on each other party; and

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > PAYMENT INTO COURT UNDER AN ORDER, ETC] (3) file at the court –

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > PAYMENT INTO COURT UNDER AN ORDER, ETC] (a) a copy of the form 100; and

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > PAYMENT INTO COURT UNDER AN ORDER, ETC] (b) a certificate of service confirming service of a copy of that form on each party served.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > PAYMENT INTO COURT UNDER AN ORDER, ETC] 1.2 Instead of complying with paragraph 1.1(1), a litigant in person without a current account may, in a claim proceeding in a county court or District Registry, make a payment into court by –

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > PAYMENT INTO COURT UNDER AN ORDER, ETC] (1) lodging the payment in cash with the court where the case is proceeding; and

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > PAYMENT INTO COURT UNDER AN ORDER, ETC] (2) giving the court a completed Court Funds Office form 100.

## APPLICATIONS RELATING TO FUNDS IN COURT

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > APPLICATIONS RELATING TO FUNDS IN COURT] 2.1 This paragraph applies to an application relating to money or securities which have been paid into court other than an application for the payment out of the money or securities (for example, an application for money to be invested, or for payment of interest to any person).

## 2.2 An application –

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > 2.2 An application –] (1) must be made in accordance with Part 23; and

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > 2.2 An application –] (2) may be made without notice, but the court may direct notice to be served on any person.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > 2.2 An application –] (Where money paid into court is accepted by or on behalf of a child or protected party, rule 21.11(1)(b) provides that the money shall be dealt with in accordance with directions given by the court under that rule and not otherwise. Paragraphs (4) to (10) of rule 21.11 make further provision about how the money may be dealt with).

## PAYMENT OUT OF COURT

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > PAYMENT OUT OF COURT] 3.1 Rule 37.3 provides that the court’s permission is required to take money out of court except where the defendant agrees that the money which has been paid into court should be used to satisfy a Part 36 offer.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > PAYMENT OUT OF COURT] 3.2 Permission may be obtained by making an application in accordance with Part 23. The application notice must state the grounds on which the order for payment out is sought. Evidence of any facts on which the applicant relies may also be necessary.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > PAYMENT OUT OF COURT] 3.3 Where the court gives permission under rule 37.3, it will include a direction for the payment out of any money in court, including any interest accrued.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > PAYMENT OUT OF COURT] 3.4 Where permission is not required to take money out of court, the requesting party should file a request for payment in Court Funds Office form 201 with the Court Funds Office, accompanied by a statement that the defendant agrees that the money should be used to satisfy the Part 36 offer in Court Funds Office form 202.

## 3.5 The request for payment should contain the following details –

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > 3.5 The request for payment should contain the following details –] (1) where the party receiving the payment is legally represented –

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > 3.5 The request for payment should contain the following details –] (a) the name, business address and reference of the legal representative; and

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > 3.5 The request for payment should contain the following details –] (b) the name of the bank and the sort code number, the title of the account and the account number where the payment is to be transmitted;

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > 3.5 The request for payment should contain the following details –] (2) where the party is acting in person –

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > 3.5 The request for payment should contain the following details –] (a) their name and address; and

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > 3.5 The request for payment should contain the following details –] (b) their bank account details as in paragraph (1)(b) above; and

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > 3.5 The request for payment should contain the following details –] (3) whether the party receiving the payment is, or has been, in receipt of services funded by the Legal Services Commission as part of the Community Legal Service.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > 3.5 The request for payment should contain the following details –] 3.6 Where paragraph 3.4 applies, interest accruing up to the date of acceptance will be paid to the defendant.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > 3.5 The request for payment should contain the following details –] (Rule 20.2 provides that in these Rules references to a claimant or defendant include a party bringing or defending an additional claim).

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > 3.5 The request for payment should contain the following details –] 3.7 Subject to paragraph 3.8, if a party does not wish the payment to be transmitted into their bank account or if they do not have a bank account, they may send a written request to the Accountant-General for the payment to be made to them by cheque.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > 3.5 The request for payment should contain the following details –] 3.8 Where a party seeking payment out of court has provided the necessary information, the payment –

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > 3.5 The request for payment should contain the following details –] (1) where a party is legally represented, must be made to the legal representative;

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > 3.5 The request for payment should contain the following details –] (2) if the party is not legally represented but has given notice under paragraph 3.5(3), must be made to the Legal Services Commission.

## PAYMENT INTO COURT BY LIFE ASSURANCE COMPANY

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > PAYMENT INTO COURT BY LIFE ASSURANCE COMPANY] 4.1 A company wishing to make a payment into court under the Life Assurance Companies (Payment into Court) Act 1896 (‘the 1896 Act’) must file a witness statement or an affidavit setting out –

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > PAYMENT INTO COURT BY LIFE ASSURANCE COMPANY] (1) a short description of the policy under which money is payable;

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > PAYMENT INTO COURT BY LIFE ASSURANCE COMPANY] (2) a statement of the persons entitled under the policy, including their names and addresses so far as known to the company;

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > PAYMENT INTO COURT BY LIFE ASSURANCE COMPANY] (3) a short statement of –

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > PAYMENT INTO COURT BY LIFE ASSURANCE COMPANY] (a) the notices received by the company making any claim to the money assured, or withdrawing any such claim;

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > PAYMENT INTO COURT BY LIFE ASSURANCE COMPANY] (b) the dates of receipt of such notices; and

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > PAYMENT INTO COURT BY LIFE ASSURANCE COMPANY] (c) the names and addresses of the persons by whom they were given;

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > PAYMENT INTO COURT BY LIFE ASSURANCE COMPANY] (4) a statement that, in the opinion of the board of directors of the company, no sufficient discharge can be obtained for the money which is payable, other than by paying it into court under the 1896 Act;

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > PAYMENT INTO COURT BY LIFE ASSURANCE COMPANY] (5) a statement that the company agrees to comply with any order or direction the court may make –

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > PAYMENT INTO COURT BY LIFE ASSURANCE COMPANY] (a) to pay any further sum into court; or

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > PAYMENT INTO COURT BY LIFE ASSURANCE COMPANY] (b) to pay any costs;

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > PAYMENT INTO COURT BY LIFE ASSURANCE COMPANY] (6) an undertaking by the company to immediately send to the Accountant General at the Court Funds Office any notice of claim received by the company after the witness statement or affidavit has been filed, together with a letter referring to the Court Funds Office reference number; and

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > PAYMENT INTO COURT BY LIFE ASSURANCE COMPANY] (7) the company’s address for service.

## 4.2 The witness statement or affidavit must be filed at –

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > 4.2 The witness statement or affidavit must be filed at –] (1) Chancery Chambers at the Royal Courts of Justice, or

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > 4.2 The witness statement or affidavit must be filed at –] (2) a Chancery district registry of the High Court.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > 4.2 The witness statement or affidavit must be filed at –] 4.3 The company must not deduct from the money payable by it under the policy any costs of the payment into court, except for any court fee.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > 4.2 The witness statement or affidavit must be filed at –] 4.4 If the company is a party to any proceedings issued in relation to the policy or the money assured by it, it may not make a payment into court under the 1896 Act without the permission of the court in those proceedings.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > 4.2 The witness statement or affidavit must be filed at –] 4.5 If a company pays money into court under the 1896 Act, unless the court orders otherwise it must immediately serve notice of the payment on every person who is entitled under the policy or has made a claim to the money assured.

## APPLICATION FOR PAYMENT OUT OF MONEY PAID INTO COURT BY LIFE ASSURANCE COMPANY

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > APPLICATION FOR PAYMENT OUT OF MONEY PAID INTO COURT BY LIFE ASSURANCE COMPANY] 5.1 Any application for the payment out of money which has been paid into court under the 1896 Act must be made in accordance with paragraph 3 of this practice direction.

## 5.2 The application must be served on –

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > 5.2 The application must be served on –] (1) every person stated in the written evidence of the company which made the payment to be entitled to or to have an interest in the money;

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > 5.2 The application must be served on –] (2) any other person who has given notice of a claim to the money; and

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > 5.2 The application must be served on –] (3) the company which made the payment, if an application is being made for costs against it, but not otherwise.

## PAYMENT INTO COURT UNDER TRUSTEE ACT 1925

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > PAYMENT INTO COURT UNDER TRUSTEE ACT 1925] 6.1 A trustee wishing to make a payment into court under section 63 of the Trustee Act 1925 must file a witness statement or an affidavit setting out –

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > PAYMENT INTO COURT UNDER TRUSTEE ACT 1925] (1) a short description of –

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > PAYMENT INTO COURT UNDER TRUSTEE ACT 1925] (a) the trust; and

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > PAYMENT INTO COURT UNDER TRUSTEE ACT 1925] (b) the instrument creating the trust, or the circumstances in which the trust arose;

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > PAYMENT INTO COURT UNDER TRUSTEE ACT 1925] (2) the names of the persons interested in or entitled to the money or securities to be paid into court, with their address so far as known to him;

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > PAYMENT INTO COURT UNDER TRUSTEE ACT 1925] (3) a statement that the trustee agrees to answer any inquiries which the court may make or direct relating to the application of the money or securities; and

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > PAYMENT INTO COURT UNDER TRUSTEE ACT 1925] (4) the trustee’s address for service.

## 6.2 The witness statement or affidavit must be filed at –

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > 6.2 The witness statement or affidavit must be filed at –] (1) Chancery Chambers at the Royal Courts of Justice;

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > 6.2 The witness statement or affidavit must be filed at –] (2) a Chancery district registry of the High Court; or

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > 6.2 The witness statement or affidavit must be filed at –] (3) the County Court hearing centre where the case is proceeding.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > 6.2 The witness statement or affidavit must be filed at –] 6.3 If a trustee pays money or securities into court, unless the court orders otherwise they must immediately serve notice of the payment into court on every person interested in or entitled to the money or securities.

## APPLICATION FOR PAYMENT OUT OF FUNDS PAID INTO COURT BY TRUSTEE

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > APPLICATION FOR PAYMENT OUT OF FUNDS PAID INTO COURT BY TRUSTEE] 7.1 An application for the payment out of any money or securities paid into court under section 63 of the Trustee Act 1925 must be made in accordance with paragraph 3 of this practice direction.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > APPLICATION FOR PAYMENT OUT OF FUNDS PAID INTO COURT BY TRUSTEE] 7.2 The application may be made without notice, but the court may direct notice to be served on any person.

## PAYMENT INTO COURT UNDER VEHICULAR ACCESS ACROSS COMMON AND OTHER LAND (ENGLAND) REGULATIONS 2002

## 8.1 In this section of this Practice Direction –

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > 8.1 In this section of this Practice Direction –] (1) expressions used have the meanings given by the Vehicular Access Across Common and Other Land (England) Regulations 2002; and

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > 8.1 In this section of this Practice Direction –] (2) a regulation referred to by number alone means the regulation so numbered in those Regulations.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > 8.1 In this section of this Practice Direction –] 8.2 Where the applicant wishes to pay money into a county court under regulation 14 they must file a witness statement or an affidavit when they lodge the money.

## 8.3 The witness statement or affidavit must –

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > 8.3 The witness statement or affidavit must –] (1) state briefly why the applicant is making the payment into court; and

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > 8.3 The witness statement or affidavit must –] (2) be accompanied by copies of –

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > 8.3 The witness statement or affidavit must –] (a) the notice served under regulation 6;

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > 8.3 The witness statement or affidavit must –] (b) any counter-notice served under regulation 8;

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > 8.3 The witness statement or affidavit must –] (c) any amended notice or counter-notice served under regulation 9;

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > 8.3 The witness statement or affidavit must –] (d) any determination of the Lands Tribunal of a matter referred to it under regulation 10; and

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > 8.3 The witness statement or affidavit must –] (e) any determination of the value of the premises by a chartered surveyor following the service of a valuation notice under regulation 12.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > 8.3 The witness statement or affidavit must –] 8.4 If an applicant pays money into court under regulation 14, he must immediately serve notice of the payment and a copy of the witness statement or affidavit on the land owner.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 37 > 8.3 The witness statement or affidavit must –] 8.5 An application for payment out of the money must be made in accordance with paragraph 3 of this practice direction.
